content.user_title: Evaluate Scholarly Work with Structured Rubrics
content.value_statement: Scholarly review can be inconsistent when criteria are unclear. This skill applies structured ScholarEval dimensions to produce balanced scores, evidence, and revision priorities.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates research work across problem formulation, literature review, methods, data, analysis, results, writing, and citations.
Provides qualitative strengths, weaknesses, critical issues, and prioritized recommendations for revision.
Supports optional 1 to 5 scoring for each applicable evaluation dimension.
Calculates weighted aggregate scores from dimension ratings with the included Python helper.
Adapts evaluation expectations for drafts, proposals, journal articles, conference papers, and student work.
limitations: It does not replace domain expert peer review for specialized technical claims.
Scores depend on the evaluator supplying accurate evidence from the scholarly work.
Some dimensions may not apply to theoretical papers or early research ideas.
The referenced schematic generation workflow depends on a separate skill or script not included here.

use_cases.title: Review a Manuscript Before Submission
use_cases.description: Assess a paper against research quality dimensions and identify high-impact revisions before journal or conference submission.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a Research Proposal
use_cases.description: Check question clarity, feasibility, methodology, contribution, and risks before funding review or thesis committee feedback.

use_cases.title: Grade Scholarly Writing Consistently
use_cases.description: Use a repeatable rubric to give structured feedback on literature reviews, thesis chapters, or seminar papers.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Paper Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single manuscript.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this scholarly paper using the ScholarEval dimensions. Focus on strengths, weaknesses, and three priority revisions.

prompt_templates.title: Dimension Scorecard
prompt_templates.prompt: Score each applicable ScholarEval dimension from 1 to 5. Explain each score with evidence from the paper and list missing information.

prompt_templates.title: Publication Readiness Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for a target venue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this manuscript for publication readiness for the target venue. Compare rigor, contribution, writing, and citations against expected standards.

prompt_templates.title: Revision Strategy Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Re-evaluate the revised draft against prior feedback. Identify remaining weaknesses, score changes, and the next highest-impact revisions.

output_examples.input: A draft empirical research paper with methods, results, and references.
output_examples.output: A structured evaluation report with dimension scores, evidence-based strengths, critical weaknesses, and prioritized revision recommendations.

output_examples.input: A grant proposal with research aims and a planned methodology.
output_examples.output: A feasibility and contribution assessment covering research questions, design quality, risks, and reviewer-facing improvement priorities.

output_examples.input: A literature review chapter for a thesis.
output_examples.output: Feedback on coverage, synthesis quality, gap identification, citation balance, organization, and writing clarity.

best_practices: Define the work type, stage, and target venue before scoring.
Support every score with specific evidence from the manuscript.
Prioritize recommendations by scholarly impact and revision effort.
anti_patterns: Do not score dimensions that are not applicable without explaining why.
Do not treat the aggregate score as a substitute for expert judgment.
Do not give vague feedback that lacks examples or revision actions.

faq.question: What types of scholarly work can it evaluate?
faq.answer: It can evaluate research papers, proposals, literature reviews, thesis chapters, conference abstracts, and similar academic drafts.

faq.question: Does it provide numeric scores?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports optional 1 to 5 scores for each applicable ScholarEval dimension.

faq.question: Can it calculate an overall score?
faq.answer: Yes. The included Python helper can calculate weighted aggregate scores from a dimension score file.

faq.question: Does it replace peer review?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured feedback, but specialized claims still need expert review.

faq.question: Can it adapt to different disciplines?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks evaluators to account for discipline norms, work stage, and venue expectations.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
